headline: Your X-ray showed moderate wear-and-tear arthritis in your right knee, and Dr. Okafor recommended physical therapy as the first step.

followUps.title: Book physical therapy
followUps.detail: Dr. Okafor plans to refer you for physical therapy twice a week for 6 weeks. When you book with the clinic on Maple Avenue, ask the front desk about early morning or evening times so Lisa can drive you.

followUps.title: Book a follow-up with Dr. Okafor
followUps.detail: See Dr. Okafor again to check how your knee is doing after physical therapy.

instructions.text: Do the home exercises your physical therapist gives you. Dr. Okafor said these exercises are the part that makes the most difference. Most people notice improvement after 4 to 6 weeks of exercises.

Take up to 2 acetaminophen tablets (500 mg each) up to 3 times a day. Do not take more than 3,000 mg in a day. Take it regularly rather than waiting until the pain is bad. Try taking a dose about an hour before physical therapy.
Do not switch to Celebrex or take your friend's tablets. Dr. Okafor said Celebrex has the same blood pressure and kidney concerns as naproxen.
Use a warm pack in the morning for stiffness. If your knee is swollen in the evening, use ice for 15 minutes.
On bad days, use a cane in your left hand to take weight off your right knee. Your physical therapist can fit you for one.
Call Dr. Okafor's office if your knee becomes hot, red, and very swollen, or if you can't put weight on it.

unchanged.text: Keep taking acetaminophen as Dr. Smith told you.
Stay off naproxen. Dr. Okafor agreed with Dr. Smith's decision to stop it because of your blood pressure.

openQuestions.text: Will you need a steroid injection in your knee?
openQuestions.resolvesWhen: Dr. Okafor can discuss it at your 3-month follow-up if your knee is still bothering you a lot after physical therapy.
